# Add forecasts from the sweep package

`fg_sweep` Augments a
[`sweep::sw_sweep()`](https://business-science.github.io/sweep/reference/sw_sweep.html)
output into
[`fgts_dygraph()`](https://derekholmes0.github.io/FinanceGraphs/reference/fgts_dygraph.md)
`forecastdataset` format. See [Introduction to
Sweep](https://business-science.github.io/sweep/articles/SW00_Introduction_to_sweep.html)

## Usage

``` r
fg_sweep(swept_data, confidence = 80)
```

## Arguments

- swept_data:

  Data resulting from a
  [`sweep::sw_sweep()`](https://business-science.github.io/sweep/reference/sw_sweep.html)
  call

- confidence:

  (Default: 80) Confidence interval (in percent) to display

## Value

`data.table` suitable for passing into
[`fgts_dygraph()`](https://derekholmes0.github.io/FinanceGraphs/reference/fgts_dygraph.md)
via the `forecastdataset` parameter

## Details

Forecast Helpers

## Examples

``` r
if (
    requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE) &
    requireNamespace("timetk", quietly = TRUE) &
    requireNamespace("sweep", quietly = TRUE)
) {
fcst_eqtypx <- timetk::tk_ts(eqtypx[,.(date,QQQ)]) |> forecast::ets() |>
      forecast::forecast(h=30) |> sweep::sw_sweep(timetk_idx=TRUE)
fcst_in <- fg_sweep(fcst_eqtypx)
toplot <- eqtypx[,.(date,IBM,QQQ)]
fgts_dygraph(toplot,title="With Forecasts", roller=1,dtstartfrac=0.7,forecast_ds=fcst_in)
}
```
